challenged_statement: A universal bound sup_b ||p_{Q3|Q'=b}||_infinity <= C follows from the full target hypotheses when Q3 is a three-large-eigenvalue spectral core and Q' the scalar residual quadratic form.
counterexample_scope: X_i iid Uniform[0,1], n=4, Hadamard spectral coordinates, A=T^T diag(1,1,-1,1/128) T. This is target-valid and has three eigenvalues of magnitude at least one.
proof_summary: For Y4=2-delta, the original cube section is a 3-simplex and (Y1,Y2,Y3)=delta times a fixed random vector. Hence Q3|Y4=(2-delta) equals delta^2 W in law and is supported on an interval of length at most 3 delta^2, so its density sup is at least 1/(3 delta^2). Since Q'=(1/128)Y4^2 is injective on Y4 in [0,2], sup_b of the conditional density norm is infinite. The full form is not a QFORM counterexample: every physical 3x3 principal minor has determinant -129/512, so the prior physical-triple theorem gives a finite universal bound for this form.
replacement: Use the scalar-residual weighted average E_{Q'} ||p_{Q3|Q'}||_infinity rather than a pointwise supremum. On the same construction the edge marginal satisfies p_{Y4}(2-delta)=(8/3)delta^3, so the rank-three coarea cap weighted by this marginal is O(delta) and integrable.
